projectDetails.name: Helium
projectDetails.description: Helium is a decentralized wireless network that incentivizes users to deploy hotspots and provide IoT and 5G coverage in exchange for crypto rewards.

topRisks.content: Lack of continuous on-chain monitoring lets abnormal fund flows go undetected, increasing the risk of delayed incident response.
The lack of a structured Bug Bounty program reduces proactive vulnerability discovery, raising the risk that attackers find issues first.
Missing CCSS certification leaves crypto custody controls unvalidated, increasing the risk of undetected security gaps.

reviews.text: Helium is a DePIN for IoT networks, using the HNT token. Launched in 2019, hotspots earn rewards. In 2025, it has 5G and mobile expansions. Community-built.

Helium is a decentralized wireless network originally built for LoRa (Long Range) IoT (Internet of things) devices and now expanding into 5G. Ordinary people deploy hotspots and earn HNT tokens for providing coverage. In 2023 Helium migrated its blockchain to Solana for more speed. It has partnerships with different carriers (for example T-Mobile for Helium Mobile) and keeps rewarding hotspot deployments. Nowadays there are thousands of hotspots worldwide with real mobile data traffic. Its on-chain changes (HIP-138) tie HNT to network utility, 100 HNT now auto-burn to buy data credits, so in order to use it, you must burn HNT. In my point of view is one the disruptive use of the blockchain with a real use case and used worldwide.

Helium is one of the most ambitious people powered networks I’ve seen it uses individuals’ devices to create wireless coverage initially for IoT via LoRaWAN. I find that vision really cool; it decentralizes infrastructure. For me, a big plus is that hotspot operators run their own LoRa servers, which helps security and censorship resistance. However, the project has faced growing pains. Usage of Helium’s token has flattened and its market cap ranking dropped a lot, indicating that interest has waned. It feels like a work in progress more than a finished product.

Helium is a decentralized wireless network that lets individuals set up "hotspots" to provide long-range, low power connectivity for IoT (Internet of Things) devices. In return, operators of these hotspots earn Helium’s native token, HNT. The network aims to reduce reliance on traditional telecom infrastructure by crowdsourcing wireless coverage and data from individuals.
